boundary_assessment: The actual helper used workspace-write, approval_policy=never, inner network disabled and temporary-directory write exceptions excluded. The probe first checks UID 1000, zero effective capabilities, no-new-privileges, no Docker socket and an ordinary outside-workspace write. Exact helper commands, errors and return codes are retained in sandbox.json.

Bubblewrap reports namespace creation denied under the tested Docker/runner restrictions; the exact enforcing kernel/seccomp/AppArmor mechanism was not isolated. The explicitly tested deprecated Landlock backend rejects this policy as requiring direct runtime enforcement. Neither probe reaches its intended inner write/network assertions, so the inner boundary is not qualified.

The outer container kept default seccomp, cap_drop=ALL, no-new-privileges, CPU/memory/PID limits and no host Docker socket. The sandbox probe was offline; a live API-connected agent did not run. Codex inner sandbox and outer container protection are separate. No protection was relaxed.

Harbor import_path is the supported extension point. The small trial subclass replaces the stock bypass flag with --sandbox workspace-write -c approval_policy=never, requires the pinned preinstalled CLI and uses a build-owned private home. The transformation is unit tested; no effective live command/config was produced. No installed upstream file changed.

assessment: The workflow successfully installed and dependency-checked the released Harbor host runtime and verified Compose. It staged 16 controls, then terminated without recoverable fixture results. Installation is not evidence of trustworthy grading.

The wrapper buffered native output in a runner-local file. When the job terminated, upload steps did not execute, so no native diagnostics or grading sidecars survived. The retained code now streams credential-free native output to the Actions log and allowlists partial results for upload, but that correction has not been exercised in another native campaign.

Paid expansion stopped because the stock Codex launcher disables its inner sandbox and the inspected rollout limit does not bound all billable input or the in-flight response. No workaround, custom cost proxy, framework fork or paid retry was introduced.

Skill activation, instruction following, correctness, seeded-defect detection, safety regressions, efficiency gains and revision improvement all remain unmeasured. A file read, favorable completion message or numeric reward cannot substitute for this evidence.

The smallest next step is one credential-free known-good task with streamed logs and recoverable checkpoints, plus qualification of a sandbox-preserving Codex launch and complete spending accounting before any paid discovery. These are prerequisites, not a recommendation to expand this trial now.
